name: Ashwagandha
doshaEffect: Balances Vata and Kapha; may increase Pitta in excess
description: Ashwagandha is one of the most important Rasayana herbs in Ayurveda. The name means 'smell of horse', referring to its unique smell and its ability to give the strength and vitality of a horse. It is a powerful adaptogen that helps the body cope with stress.
benefits: Reduces stress and anxiety by supporting adrenal function
Improves strength, stamina and muscle mass
Supports healthy sleep and reduces insomnia
Enhances male reproductive health and vitality
traditionalUses: As a general tonic after illness
modernApplications: Adaptogen for chronic stress and burnout
Supportive in mild anxiety and sleep issues
dosage: Root powder: 3–6 g daily with warm milk or ghee. Capsules: 300–600 mg standardized extract twice daily. Best taken at night or as directed by practitioner.
precautions: Avoid in high Pitta conditions, pregnancy (unless supervised), and hyperthyroidism. May interact with sedatives and thyroid medications. Consult doctor if on medication.
howToUse: Mix 1 tsp powder in warm milk with a pinch of turmeric and honey (after cooling). Can also be taken as tea or in ghee preparations (Ashwagandha Ghrita).

name: Tulsi
doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Vata; may increase Pitta in excess
description: Tulsi is revered as the 'Queen of Herbs' and a sacred plant in Hindu tradition. It is a powerful adaptogen and immune modulator used for thousands of years for respiratory health, stress, and spiritual purity.
benefits: Supports respiratory health and clears congestion
Reduces stress and promotes mental clarity
Purifies the mind and environment (traditional belief)
modernApplications: Natural support for seasonal allergies and colds
dosage: Fresh leaves: 5–10 leaves daily. Dried leaf powder: 1–2 g. Tea: 1 tsp dried leaves steeped in hot water 5–10 min, 2–3 times daily.
precautions: Avoid large amounts in pregnancy. May thin blood – caution with anticoagulants. High doses may lower blood sugar.
howToUse: Chew 4–5 fresh leaves every morning. Make tea with ginger and honey for colds. Use as steam inhalation for congestion.

name: Turmeric
doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Pitta; may increase Vata in excess
description: Turmeric is the golden spice of Ayurveda, used both as medicine and food. Its active compound curcumin gives it powerful anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. It is considered one of the best blood purifiers.
benefits: Supports joint health and reduces pain
Purifies blood and improves skin health
traditionalUses: As a daily spice for health
dosage: Powder: 1–3 g daily with black pepper and fat (ghee/milk) for better absorption. Golden milk: ½ tsp turmeric + pinch black pepper in warm milk.
precautions: High doses may cause stomach upset. Caution in gallstones, bile duct obstruction, and before surgery (blood thinning). Avoid excessive use in pregnancy.
howToUse: Golden milk at night. Mix with honey for wounds (external). Add to all cooking. Combine with black pepper and oil/ghee.

name: Amla
rasa: Amla (Sour) predominant; has all five tastes except Lavana (Salty)
doshaEffect: Tridoshic – balances all three Doshas (especially Pitta)
description: Amla is considered the best Rasayana in Ayurveda and one of the richest natural sources of Vitamin C. It is a key ingredient in Triphala and Chyawanprash. Called 'Dhatri' meaning 'the nurse' for its nourishing qualities.
benefits: Highest natural source of Vitamin C and antioxidants
Promotes hair growth and prevents graying
Balances blood sugar and supports liver
dosage: Fresh fruit: 1 medium daily. Powder: 3–6 g. Juice: 10–20 ml diluted. Best taken in morning.
precautions: Generally very safe. Excess may increase dryness in high Vata. Fresh juice is preferred over heat-processed products for Vitamin C.
howToUse: Eat fresh when in season. Amla murabba. Mix powder with honey. Key ingredient in Triphala and Chyawanprash.

name: Brahmi
doshaEffect: Balances Vata and Pitta; slightly increases Kapha
description: Brahmi is the premier Medhya Rasayana (brain tonic) of Ayurveda. Named after Brahma, the creator, it is traditionally used to enhance memory, intellect, concentration and calm the mind.
dosage: Powder: 1–3 g twice daily with ghee or milk. Fresh juice: 10–20 ml. Standardized extract: as per label (often 300 mg).
precautions: Generally safe. May cause digestive upset in high doses. Caution in bradycardia. Consult if on thyroid or sedative medication.
howToUse: Brahmi ghrita (medicated ghee) is classical. Fresh juice with honey. Tea from dried leaves. Oil for head massage (Brahmi Taila).

name: Shatavari
doshaEffect: Balances Pitta and Vata; increases Kapha
prabhava: Stanya (promotes breast milk), Rasayana for women
description: Shatavari means 'she who possesses a hundred husbands', reflecting its traditional use as a female reproductive tonic. It is the primary Rasayana for women in Ayurveda, supporting hormonal balance, fertility and lactation.
benefits: Supports female reproductive health and hormonal balance
Promotes healthy lactation in nursing mothers
Nourishes and cools the body (Pitta pacifying)
Supports digestive comfort and soothes acidity
Acts as a mild adaptogen and immune supporter
dosage: Root powder: 3–6 g twice daily with milk or ghee. Capsules: 500 mg standardized, 1–2 times daily.
precautions: Avoid in high Kapha conditions, edema, or congestion. May not suit those with estrogen-sensitive conditions without guidance.
howToUse: Cook with milk and ghee as a rejuvenative. Mix powder in warm milk at night. Classical preparations include Shatavari Ghrita.

name: Neem
doshaEffect: Balances Pitta and Kapha; increases Vata
description: Neem is called the 'Village Pharmacy' because almost every part of the tree has medicinal use. It is one of the most powerful blood purifiers and antimicrobial herbs in Ayurveda.
benefits: Excellent blood purifier and skin healer
Promotes oral health (twigs traditionally used as toothbrush)
Helps manage skin conditions like acne and eczema
dosage: Leaf powder: 1–3 g. Leaf juice: 10–20 ml. Oil: external use mainly. Bark decoction for internal use under guidance.
precautions: Very bitter – not for long-term high-dose use without guidance. Avoid in high Vata, pregnancy, and infertility concerns. Seed oil is toxic internally in high amounts.
howToUse: Neem leaf tea or powder with honey. External paste for skin. Neem oil diluted for scalp and skin. Chew neem sticks for oral health.

name: Triphala
botanicalName: Terminalia chebula + Terminalia bellirica + Emblica officinalis
partsUsed: Dried fruits of Haritaki, Bibhitaki, Amalaki
rasa: All six tastes (predominantly astringent, bitter, sweet, sour)
doshaEffect: Tridoshic – gently balances all three Doshas
prabhava: Best mild laxative and rejuvenative for digestion and eyes
description: Triphala is the most famous compound formula in Ayurveda – equal parts of Haritaki, Bibhitaki and Amalaki. It is a gentle yet effective cleanser, rejuvenator and eye tonic used for centuries.
benefits: Rejuvenates the colon and gut lining
dosage: Powder: 1–3 g at night with warm water. Tablets: as directed. Start low to assess tolerance.
precautions: May cause loose stools initially. Reduce dose if too strong. Not for severe diarrhea or dehydration. Safe for long-term use at appropriate dose.
howToUse: Take ½–1 tsp powder in warm water at bedtime. Can also be used as a wash for eyes (filtered decoction) or mouth rinse.

name: Guduchi
description: Guduchi is called 'Amrita' meaning nectar of immortality. It is one of the most important immune-modulating and detoxifying herbs in Ayurveda, used for fever, infections and as a general rejuvenative.
benefits: Supports recovery from fever and infections
dosage: Stem powder/decoction: 3–6 g or 20–30 ml decoction twice daily. Satva (starch extract): 500 mg–1 g.
precautions: Generally safe. High doses may cause constipation in some. Consult practitioner in autoimmune conditions and pregnancy.
howToUse: Decoction of stem. Guduchi satva with honey. Often combined with other herbs in classical formulas.

name: Arjuna
doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Pitta; may increase Vata
description: Arjuna is the foremost cardiac tonic (Hridya) in Ayurveda. The bark has been used for centuries to support heart strength, circulation and emotional healing related to the heart.
benefits: Strengthens heart muscle and supports cardiac function
Supports healthy blood pressure and cholesterol
dosage: Bark powder: 1–3 g twice daily with milk or water. Decoction: 20–30 ml. Standardized extracts as directed.
precautions: Generally safe. Monitor if on cardiac medications. Consult doctor before use in heart conditions.
howToUse: Bark decoction with milk. Powder mixed in warm milk. Classical Arjuna Ksheerapaka (milk decoction).

name: Haritaki
rasa: All five tastes except Lavana (predominantly Kashaya)
prabhava: Best among fruits for detoxification and longevity
description: Haritaki is called the 'King of Medicines' in Tibetan medicine and is highly revered in Ayurveda. It is one of the three fruits of Triphala and is considered a powerful rejuvenative and eliminator of toxins.
benefits: Rejuvenates the body and promotes longevity
traditionalUses: As a daily Rasayana (especially for Vata)
dosage: Powder: 1–3 g at night. Different preparations for different effects (with salt, honey, ghee, etc.).
precautions: Avoid in pregnancy and severe debility without guidance. May cause dryness if overused.
howToUse: Classic: different Anupana (vehicles) change its effect. With rock salt for Kapha, with ghee for Vata, with honey for Pitta.

name: Ginger
doshaEffect: Balances Vata and Kapha; increases Pitta
description: Ginger is one of the most widely used spices and medicines in Ayurveda. Fresh (Ardraka) and dry (Shunthi) have slightly different properties. It is the best herb for kindling Agni (digestive fire).
benefits: Warms the body and improves circulation
Supports respiratory health and clears Kapha
Helps in motion sickness and morning sickness
modernApplications: Nausea of pregnancy and chemotherapy support
dosage: Fresh: 1–2 g grated in tea. Dry powder: 1–2 g. With honey for Kapha, with rock salt for Vata.
precautions: Avoid high doses in high Pitta, peptic ulcers, and before surgery. May increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants.
howToUse: Ginger tea with lemon and honey. Fresh ginger with salt before meals. Dry ginger in cooking and formulas (Trikatu).

name: Guggulu
doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Vata; increases Pitta
description: Guggulu is a powerful resin used for its scraping (Lekhana) and fat-reducing properties. It is central to many classical formulas for joints, cholesterol and weight management.
benefits: Supports healthy cholesterol and lipid levels
Helps in weight management by reducing Meda (fat tissue)
traditionalUses: As a carrier (Yogavahi) in many formulas
dosage: Purified Guggulu: 500 mg–1 g twice daily with warm water or as in compound formulas. Always use purified (Shuddha) Guggulu.
precautions: Must be purified before use. Avoid in high Pitta, pregnancy, and kidney disorders. May interact with some medications. Use under guidance.
howToUse: Almost always used in classical compound formulas (Yogas) rather than alone. Examples: Yograj Guggulu, Kaishore Guggulu, Kanchanar Guggulu.

name: Yashtimadhu
doshaEffect: Balances Vata and Pitta; increases Kapha
description: Yashtimadhu is the classic soothing, sweet herb of Ayurveda. It is widely used for throat, respiratory tract, digestion and as a harmonizer in many formulas.
benefits: Soothes throat, cough and respiratory tract
Acts as a natural sweetener and harmonizer
traditionalUses: As a base in many herbal formulas
dosage: Powder: 1–3 g. Decoction: 20–30 ml. Often combined with other herbs. Not for continuous high-dose long-term use.
precautions: Avoid prolonged high doses – can cause hypertension, edema, and potassium loss (pseudoaldosteronism). Contraindicated in hypertension, kidney disease, pregnancy (high dose), and with certain medications.
howToUse: Decoction or powder with honey for cough. Classic ingredient in many Kwaths and Ghritas. External paste for skin.

name: Bhringraj
doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Vata; increases Pitta
description: Bhringraj is the foremost herb for hair in Ayurveda. Its name means 'ruler of the hair'. It is also an important liver tonic and rejuvenative for the mind.
benefits: Promotes hair growth and prevents premature graying
Strengthens hair roots and improves hair quality
Acts as a mild brain tonic
modernApplications: Hair oils and hair growth serums
dosage: Leaf juice: 10–20 ml. Powder: 1–3 g. Oil: external application on scalp.
precautions: Generally safe. High doses may increase Pitta. Consult in liver disease and pregnancy.
howToUse: Fresh leaf juice applied on scalp. Bhringraj oil for head massage. Internal use as powder or juice with honey.
